newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GBL offers SGB control of Tractebel - paper.
newsitem.headline: GBL offers SGB control of Tractebel - paper.

text.p: Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) and its affiliated companies want to sell their stake in utility Tractebel to holding Ste Generale de Belgique (SGB), the Financieel Economische Tijd newspaper said on Tuesday.
"(GBL chairman) Baron (Albert) Frere is offering Societe Generale absolute power over Tractebel," the Tijd said.
SGB was not immediately available for comment.
The Tijd said the issue would be discussed at a meeting of SGB's executive committee later on Tuesday.
Neither Tractebel nor GBL were available for comment.
Also on the agenda is a decision as to whether Generale de Banque, in which SGB has a 29.6 percent stake, could boost its capital by a substantial amount, the Tijd said.
The Tijd said that the capital increase should give Generale Bank financial breathing space to respond to new opportunities.

SGB, which is 62.6 percent owned by French Cie de Suez, has a 32.67 percent direct stake in Tractebel. The GBL group, including Electrafina has 20.3 percent. Insurer Royale Belge, another affiliated company, would also sell its 4.29 percent Tractebel stake.

The newspaper said GBL chairman Albert Frere was proposing the sale at 14,500 francs per Tractebel share, which closed at 12,925 francs on the Brussels forward market on Monday. The price of the operation for SGB would be at least 50 billion francs, it said.
It said Frere had given SGB a few weeks to decide, adding he had another buyer for his Tractebel stock -- German utility group RWE AG.
But Frere and his ally Royal Belge first have to offer their shares to SGB, according to a 1989 agreement, the paper said.
